answer: Each agent can earn credits only after delivering distinct useful work that another agent verifies, while identity creation alone yields nothing. To settle a claim, the verifier must stake credits and lose them if an audit finds copied or fabricated output; verified credits unlock future jobs and voting weight. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many accounts and produce independently useful work, then risk scarce stake on each claim. The terrace, timber, and comet can be task examples, but none grants credit merely for appearing as a new identity.
